industry.structure: Industrial gases are made by separating air (oxygen, nitrogen, argon) in air separation units that run on electricity; power is the largest cash cost. Gas is sold three ways: on-site/tonnage plants built next to a big customer (steel, refinery, chemicals) on 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts with power passed through; merchant liquid delivered by cryogenic tanker within ~200-300 km of a plant; and cylinders (packaged). Liquid is costly to move, so markets are regional and local density decides returns.
industry.players: Linde India (Linde plc 75%); Praxair India (Linde plc 100%, unlisted; FY25 turnover Rs 2,771 cr); INOX Air Products (unlisted); Air Liquide India; Air Water India (bought Linde India's South Region business in 2019); Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases (listed Jul-2025, FY26 revenue Rs 342 cr) and many small regional fillers. Large steel makers also run captive ASUs, which they increasingly outsource ('de-captivation').

globalMajors.name: Linde plc
globalMajors.detail: 2025 sales ~US$34 bn and market value above US$210 bn (Linde India AGM deck, Aug-2026). Q2 2026 (31-Jul-2026): sales US$9,289 mn (+9%, underlying +4%), adjusted operating margin 29.5%, adjusted EPS US$4.50 (+10%); 2026 adjusted EPS guidance US$17.70-17.90; capex US$5.5-6.0 bn; sale-of-gas backlog US$8.1 bn. moat: On-site contracts with steel and refinery customers
Advantage

15-20 year take-or-pay supply from plants at Tata Steel (Jamshedpur, Kalinganagar), SAIL Rourkela, JSL Jajpur, IOCL Panipat; lease rentals alone Rs 127 cr in FY26 with Rs 677 cr of minimum future receipts; 'highest number of ASUs on BOO basis in India'.
Visible, contracted cash flows; switching costs are very high once a plant sits inside a customer's fence.
Regional density in East and North India
Advantage (narrowed by the allocation)

12 ASU sites, merchant ASUs at Selaqui, Ludhiana, Dahej, Jamshedpur; record merchant loading (2,360 TPD in FY26). But since Mar-2020 new merchant business in the South, Central India and Maharashtra bulk goes to Praxair India.
Local scale is the real moat in gases, and the parent has fenced off the South and Central regions.
Engineering capability (PED)
Advantage
Designs and builds ASUs in-house (Kolkata U-stamp shop, Jamshedpur workshop); wins third-party orders for India's first semiconductor fab (Tata Dholera) and OSAT; ~Rs 2,000 cr third-party order book.
Lowers its own plant cost and wins jobs, but the business is lumpy and audit flags its estimates.
Linde plc technology, safety and brand
Advantage
Global process technology, applications know-how, remote operating centres; royalty Rs 70 cr a year (2.8% of revenue) paid for it.
Real, but paid for, and available equally to the parent's 100%-owned Praxair India.
Pricing power in merchant liquid
Neutral
Merchant margins rose with tight supply (FY24-26) but INOX, Air Liquide, Air Water and Ellenbarrie add capacity; Q1FY27 gases margin slipped on power tariffs.
Cyclical; not a durable moat.
Cost position (power)
Weak
Power and fuel Rs 415 cr in FY26 (16% of revenue); 22% renewable; on-site power is passed through, merchant power is not.
No cost edge over INOX/Air Liquide.
critiques: The valuation: ~100x trailing earnings and ~55x EV/EBITDA for a business growing EPS in single digits since FY23, with ROE of 12-14%.

Minority shareholders' interests are subordinate: the parent allocated South and Central India and the HyCO/CO2 businesses to its 100%-owned Praxair India without a vote or a valuation; SAT called it a transfer of a 'profit making apparatus'.

Public shareholders have voted against the company repeatedly: 93.94% against RPTs (2021), 89% against the FY26 Praxair RPT limit (Mar-2026), ~86% of public votes against adopting the FY26 accounts (Aug-2026).
The auditor (PwC) qualified the FY26 accounts; the NSE valuer's report on 'business foregone' is undisclosed and could lead to SEBI action, compensation demands or orders on directors.
FY26 profit growth (+21%) was flattered by a Rs 90 cr reversal of liabilities and a ~Rs 49 cr JV one-off; underlying profit was roughly flat (~Rs 444 cr vs Rs 449 cr ex-exceptional in FY25).
Heavy capex (Rs 2,100 cr in FY25-26) has turned free cash flow negative and run cash down from Rs 980 cr to Rs 112 cr; returns on the new on-site plants are not disclosed.
The price may embed a corporate-action option (delisting or merger with Praxair India): minority holders demanded Rs 2,025 against a Rs 428.5 floor in 2019.
